source_text: Nullam itaque tibi calumniam commovemus, quasi damnes nuptias, et quasi hominem, qui ex illis nascitur, opus diaboli esse dicas; nec infideliter hoc obicimus, nec imperite colligimus; sed qui sit consequentium sententiarum effectus, sollicite et simpliciter intuemur. Numquam sunt enim sine commixtione nuptiae corporales. Tu dicis, quicumque ex illa commixtione nascuntur, ad diabolum pertinere; dubio procul pronuntias nuptias ad ius daemonis pertinere.
pass_a_gloss: We therefore move no calumny against you, as if you condemn marriages, and as if you say that the human who is born from them is a work of the devil; nor do we object this faithlessly, nor gather it unskillfully; but what the effect of the following sentences is, we look at carefully and simply. For never are there bodily marriages without mingling. You say that whoever are born from that mingling pertain to the devil; without doubt you pronounce that marriages pertain to the right of the demon.

lemmas.lexica: LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: We therefore bring no false accusation when we say that you condemn marriage and call the human being born from it the devil's work. We neither make this charge faithlessly nor reach this conclusion ignorantly. We simply and carefully observe what your statements entail. Bodily marriage never exists without sexual union. You say that everyone born from that union belongs to the devil. You are undoubtedly declaring that marriage belongs under the demon's authority.

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
